$comment: The half of the spec a server cannot tell us.
spec/openapi/fog-1.6.json is FOG's own description of itself: every path, every
method, every field with its type, length, nullability and required-ness, and the
permission each operation needs. It is authoritative and it is regenerated, never
edited. What it cannot know is what FogApi should call any of it, which operations
deserve a typed cmdlet at all, which ones are already hand-written and must stay
that way, and where FOG 1.5 differs. That is this file.
Kept deliberately small. Anything mechanically derivable belongs in
spec/tools/Build-FogApiSpec.ps1 as a rule, not here as 555 entries.
Terms used here -- upsert, natural key, route class, route shape, folded,
deferred, L1, emitter -- are defined in spec/README.md under Terms.
One rule, four renderings. The spec stores verb and noun separately so every
emitter derives from the same source rather than munging another emitter's
output: Get-FogHost / get_fog_host() / getFogHost / 'fogapi get-fog-host'.
Verbs are checked against Get-Verb by the builder, which fails rather than
warns. An unapproved verb reaching a released module is a PSScriptAnalyzer
error on somebody else's CI, not ours.
list and indiv are ONE cmdlet, not two. Get-Fog{Noun} answers both, the
way Get-Process and Get-Service do: no arguments returns everything, -All
says so explicitly, -id or -name narrows to one.
This replaced Get-Fog{Noun}s / Get-Fog{Noun}. Plural nouns tripped
PSUseSingularNouns, needed a pluralisation rule with a table of irregulars,
and split one question -- 'get me printers' -- across two names the caller
has to choose between. -All is the standard spelling for the same thing.
Every existing plural name survives as an alias, so nothing breaks.
Operations that become a parameter on another cmdlet rather than a cmdlet of
their own. Emitting all 554 operations would produce a module nobody can
tab-complete through, and count/names/ids are modifiers on 'list' rather than
distinct things an admin wants to do.
join was folded onto New-Fog{Noun} -Upsert here, on the strength of the
document calling it an upsert against the natural key. That was wrong, and it
was caught by trying it against a real server: PUT /{class}/join is a BULK
EDIT over an explicit ids array, and sending it a body with no ids answers 202
and changes nothing. The upsert-by-name is the POST variant, and it exists on
group alone -- every other class answers 400.
Both are now described correctly upstream (fogproject openapi.class.php), so
the snapshot no longer misleads. Modelling them in FogApi is deferred rather
than guessed at, because neither fits the shape it was folded into: a bulk
edit is a plural cmdlet taking many ids, and a group-only get-or-create is a
hand-written group helper, not a generic per-class shape.

join.reason: PUT is a bulk edit over an ids array; POST is a group-only get-or-create. Neither is a modifier on an existing cmdlet, and both want their own design. Reachable meanwhile through Update-FogObject -uri.
join.putSemantics: PUT /{class}/join with {ids:[...], <fields>} applies those field values to every listed object, leaving omitted fields alone. 202, no body. No ids means no effect.
join.postSemantics: POST /group/join with {names:[...]} returns an id per name, creating any that do not exist. 201. Group only; all other classes answer 400.

$comment: Route class name to FogApi noun. Only classes whose PascalCase is not simply
the capitalised route name need an entry; the builder title-cases the rest.
Plurals likewise: only irregular ones are listed.
The server has no get-by-name route. AltoRouter constrains the id segment
to [i:id], so /{class}/{name} does not route at all. Getting one object by
name is therefore a client-side convenience, and FogApi has always offered
it -- Get-FogHost -hostName and Get-FogGroupByName both do it, each a
different way.
The generated -name parameter resolves through /{class}/names: an unpaged,
uncapped list of id and name pairs, matched exactly, then one GET by id.
Two requests, both small.
Not /{class}/search/{item}, which is one request but matches the term
across every field -- so searching a printer named 'Alpha' also hits any
printer whose description mentions Alpha, and the result still needs
filtering. Not a full list either, which is what Get-FogHost does and which
now pages the entire table since the 1.6 paging fix.
names is 1.6 only, so on 1.5 the emitted cmdlet falls back to search.
Alternative spellings for a generated cmdlet's parameters.
These have to live here rather than in the emitted file, because the
emitter overwrites what it emits: an alias added by hand to a generated
cmdlet survives exactly until the next run, then disappears with no error.
Declaring it here is what makes it durable.
They matter more than they look. A parameter alias is the whole mechanism
for renaming a parameter without breaking callers, and the generated names
come from the server's field names, which do not always match what FogApi
already called the same thing.
Parameter aliases are NOT module aliases and never reach AliasesToExport.
PowerShell resolves them intrinsically, they survive invoke-modulebuild
into the built psm1, and Get-Help reports them so PlatyPS documents them.
All four of those were verified rather than assumed.
common applies to every generated cmdlet that has the parameter.
byClass is keyed class then parameter, for the cases where one class
already had a different name for a field.

setting.$comment: Get-FogSetting has taken -settingName since it was written. The server calls the field name, so the generated cmdlet does too, and the old spelling stays bindable.
name: settingName

$comment: Which classes get typed cmdlets, and in what order. The tier decides scope, not
naming: a tier-3 class still gets the same Get-Fog{Noun}s / Get-Fog{Noun} names,
it just does not get the four write verbs even where the server allows them,
because nobody manages a lookup table from a cmdlet.
Counts here are what the emitter will produce, derived by the builder from the
operations the snapshot actually declares for each class. They are not typed in.

5.label: Fixed routes, hand-written
$comment: No L1 representation, so these are the only cmdlets allowed to call
Invoke-FogApi directly. Named individually because a fixed route has no
class to derive a noun from.

status.note: Also serves /system/status; same handler, same payload. Carries version AND the paging bounds, which is what makes it the cheap probe.

openapi.note: Unauthenticated. The runtime half of this whole effort.

unisearch.note: -Limit is per entity type, not a total, and there is no nextUrl. Must not reuse -First.

pendingmacs.note: Existing function is host-scoped; this route is server-wide.

logfiles.note: Get-FogLog reads a LOCAL log file. This route reads the server's.

$comment: The functions that stay hand-written forever, and why. They are registered
rather than generated so the coverage matrix shows them as covered instead of
as gaps, and so the Python emitter knows which ones it owes.
category:
transport      the single HTTP choke point
l1             the generic CRUD layer everything else routes through
workflow       version branching, join-table reconciliation, multi-call
orchestration. Generating these would mean generating
judgement.
local          talks to the machine it runs on, not to FOG
utility        pure local logic, no API call
config         reads or writes the settings file
platform: any | windows | posix
targets: which emitters owe an equivalent

Invoke-FogApi.note: A cmdlet in FogApi.dll, not a file in Public/. Still hand-written -- transport is not an API operation, it is what every operation goes through -- and still owed by the python emitter; what moved is the language, not the obligation. Public/Invoke-FogApi.ps1 was deleted in the same commit that added the cmdlet, because a function beats a cmdlet in PowerShell's resolution order: with both present the .ps1 silently wins, ignores Set-FogTransport, and reaches the network.

Send-FogWolTask.note: WOL is not a route: it is task with wol true / taskTypeID 14.

New-FogTaskRequest.note: Static factory for the FogTaskRequest class. A PowerShell class is not reachable by name after Import-Module -- naming it needs `using module` -- so the type needs a cmdlet to construct it. PowerShell only: the class is a PowerShell language feature, and the other emitters model the same request body their own way.

Get-FogHost.note: Identifies the local machine when given no parameters. The pure by-id read is what the generated Get-FogHost would be, which is why this one keeps the name and the generator skips host/indiv.

Repair-FogSnapinAssociations.note: FOG enforces no integrity on association rows; this reconciles them.

Get-FogVersion.note: Probes system/info then falls back to service/getversion.php for 1.5.

Get-FogInventory.note: Splits in phase 5.5 into Get-FogLocalInventory and Get-FogHostInventory.

Set-WinToBootToPxe.note: Unifies with efibootmgr as Set-FogBootToPxe in phase 5.5.

$comment: Existing one-line wrappers over L1 that the generator would otherwise emit a
duplicate of. The generated name wins where they differ, and the existing name
becomes an alias -- never the reverse, and nothing here is deleted.
operation is the snapshot operationId these stand in for, so the coverage
matrix can mark it covered.
FOG 1.5 deltas. There is no 1.5 spec to generate from -- that line ships no
commons/schema-expected.php, so nothing describes its types -- which means the
1.5 story is hand-recorded here or it is guessed at.
Every generated cmdlet must work against both, so the emitter reads this to
decide what to branch on.
fifteen.envelope: {count, <classname>s[]} rather than 1.6's DataTables-style envelope. Add-FogResultData already normalises this.

routeSpellings.$comment: 1.6 documents PUT /{class}/{id} and DELETE /{class}/{id}; 1.5 serves only the /edit and /delete spellings. 1.6 accepts both, so the /edit spelling is the one that works on both and is what the emitter uses.

fifteen.paging: None. No limit(), no complex(), no MAX_ROWS, no paginate. The query string is ignored and lists are unbounded, so the pager collapses to one request.

absentClasses.$comment: Classes in the 1.6 snapshot that 1.5 has no route for. A generated cmdlet for one of these has to fail clearly on 1.5 rather than 404 obscurely.
